summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad Part 103 addresses the theological question of whether Prophet Muhammad physically saw Allah during the Night of Ascension (Isra). Sheikh Ali Mashhour analyzes various companion narrations and scholarly opinions, concluding that while the Prophet may have had a spiritual observation of Allah, there is no evidence of a physical, literal sight in this life. The discussion clarifies apparent contradictions in companion reports by examining the context and specificity of different questions asked. The lecture then shifts to the Prophet's detailed description of Jerusalem to the Quraysh, emphasizing how he provided accurate information about caravans and specific details that could only be known by actual presence, yet this only increased their disbelief—illustrating the principle that revelation's impact depends on the questioner's intention.
suggested_title: Did the Prophet See Allah? - Analysis of Isra Narrations and the Power of Intention in Receiving Revelation
catchy_title: Why Did Truth Increase Their Disbelief?
